answer: bonding identity: every agent posts a small time-locked deposit before it can transact, and the deposit is refunded only after the agent completes an honest epoch of activity, verified by peer attestations. A fake identity must therefore lock real collateral per persona, and slashed deposits if the persona misbehaves during its epoch, so maintaining thousands of sybils ties up capital for the whole lock duration. An attacker sweeping identities like a comet through the network earns nothing, and a gale of fresh agents gets filtered by the bonding cost, while honest agents like a steady ridge
